title: Sea Ice
supports: Explains the ice-ocean reflectivity contrast and reinforcing melt cycle, seasonal context and insulating role of sea ice, and that floating sea ice melt does not directly raise sea level.

title: Why Sea Ice Matters
publisher: National Snow and Ice Data Center
supports: Explains why bright sea ice and dark open water absorb different amounts of solar energy and how that contrast can amplify melt.

title: Chapter 10: Linking Global to Regional Climate Change
supports: Assesses ice-albedo alongside other mechanisms associated with Arctic amplification.

title: Arctic and Antarctic Sea Ice Change: Contrasts, Commonalities, and Causes
supports: Synthesizes differences between Arctic and Antarctic sea ice, the role of geography and natural variability, coupled atmosphere-ice-ocean processes, and remaining model biases.

title: Evidence for ice-ocean albedo feedback in the Arctic Ocean shifting to a seasonal ice zone
supports: Uses 1979-2014 satellite observations and a simplified upper-ocean model in the Pacific Arctic; finds early-season ice divergence can trigger albedo feedback that amplifies summer retreat, while noting the regional model scope and other contributing processes.
